bib.title: FlexGen: High-Throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 202

question: How can an LLM such as OPT-175B be run for throughput-oriented, latency-insensitive batch inference on a single commodity GPU by offloading to CPU memory and disk?
hypothesis: Throughput-oriented workloads can trade latency for large batch sizes, so a better offloading schedule, tensor placement and 4-bit compression of weights and KV cache amortize I/O and give far higher throughput than offloading systems that inherit training strategies.
contributions: A search space of offloading strategies (compute schedule, tensor placement, computation delegation) with a proof that the zig-zag block schedule is within 2x of optimal I/O complexity, and a linear-programming policy search.
4-bit group-wise quantization of weights and KV cache for OPT-175B without retraining or calibration, with negligible accuracy loss.
Evaluation on T4 GPUs showing much higher throughput than DeepSpeed ZeRO-Inference and Hugging Face Accelerate (up to 100x with compression).

method.summary: FlexGen is a PyTorch generation engine that treats GPU, CPU and disk as a three-level memory hierarchy. It uses a zig-zag block schedule that reuses loaded weights over a block of GPU batches, overlaps I/O with compute, places weights/activations/KV cache by percentages found with an LP-based cost-model search, optionally delegates attention to the CPU, and optionally compresses weights and KV cache to 4 bits (group size 64). Top-K sparse attention (10% of V cache) is shown as an additional approximation.

models.architecture: offloads whole weights to CPU or disk, row-by-row schedule, KV cache and activations on GPU

models.architecture: offloads a fraction of weights, row-by-row schedule, cache/activations on GPU

models.architecture: decentralized collaborative inference, INT8 by default

other.gpus: 1 GPU for 6.7B, 4 for 30B, 24 for 175B, per-GPU throughput reported

inference.temperature: only for HELM xsum scenario: temperature=0.3 (Table 9)
inference.max_tokens: 32 generated tokens in main benchmarks; 128, 8 in appendix runs
inference.samples: not stated; throughput benchmarks appear to be single runs with no seeds or variance reported. When a full batch is too slow for a system, fewer tokens are generated and throughput projected.
inference.prompting: synthetic padded prompts for throughput; real weights for accuracy evaluations, dummy weights for throughput

parameters.quantization: 4-bit group-wise asymmetric, group size 64; weights grouped along output channel dimension, KV cache along hidden dimension; dequantized to FP16 before compute; 3-bit did not preserve accuracy
parameters.sparse_attention: Top-K, 10% sparsity on the value cache (4-bit-S)
parameters.policy_variables: 11: block size bls, GPU batch size gbs, weight placement wg wc wd, activation placement hg hc hd, KV cache placement cg cc cd
parameters.policy_search: enumerate (bls, gbs) (gbs multiple of 4, bls less than 20), then solve LP over 9 placement variables; cost-model constants fit from profiling; policy sometimes adjusted manually after OOM
parameters.cpu_delegation: turned off when quantization is enabled
parameters.overlap: Algorithm 1 overlaps weight load of next layer, cache/activation load of next batch, store of previous batch, and compute
parameters.pipeline_parallel: layers split equally over m GPUs; micro-batch pipelining

other.cost_model: T = Tpre*l + Tgen*(n-1)*l; Tpre = max(ctog, gtoc, dtoc, ctod, comp) for prefill; Tgen likewise for decoding
other.page_cache: ablation tables 21, 22, 24 use the pagecache-management tool to disable OS disk cache; OPT-175B reads 0.49 vs 0.69 in Table 2

metrics.name: generation throughput
metrics.definition: number of generated tokens / (prefill time + decoding time), i.e. bn/t

metrics.name: decoding throughput
metrics.definition: generated tokens over decoding time only, assuming prefill is done

metrics.name: latency
metrics.definition: total seconds to process the prompts and generate all bn tokens of a block

metrics.name: padded vs actual throughput (HELM)
metrics.definition: padded: tokens in padded prompts plus padded outputs over latency; actual: non-padding tokens only

eval.protocol: Maximum throughput per system under memory limits on 1 T4 GPU (and 4 GPUs for pipeline scaling); latency-throughput Pareto frontier by tuning batch size; ablations disabling one technique at a time on OPT-30B and OPT-175B. No seeds, repeats or significance tests stated. Quantization in baselines left off (Accelerate's is incompatible with offloading, DeepSpeed's loses accuracy at 175B).

availability.data: synthetic prompts; Lambada, WikiText, HELM and data wrangling datasets are public

results.claim: FlexGen runs OPT-175B on one T4 at 0.69 token/s without compression versus 0.01 for DeepSpeed and Accelerate (prompt 512).
results.setup: OPT-175B, 1 T4 16GB, 208 GB CPU, 1.5 TB SSD, prompt 512, output 32, policy 32x8 GPU batches, weights 0% GPU 50% CPU 50% disk
results.quote: Baseline systems can only use a maximum batch size of 2, but FlexGen can use a GPU batch size of 32 and a block size of 32 × 8, achieving a 69× higher throughput.

results.claim: With 4-bit compression FlexGen reaches 1.12 token/s on OPT-175B with effective batch size 144 and no disk offloading, 112x the baselines.
results.setup: OPT-175B, 1 T4, prompt 512, output 32, weights and KV cache 4-bit, all held in CPU memory
results.quote: With compression enabled, FlexGen achieves a 112× higher generation throughput on a single GPU for prompt sequence length 512.
results.note: The introduction says 100x higher maximum throughput at effective batch size 144 with latency 4000 seconds; Section 6.1 says 112x.

results.claim: At the same 5000 s latency, FlexGen without compression gets more than 40x the throughput of DeepSpeed Zero-Inference on OPT-175B.

results.claim: FlexGen at latency 12000 s with effective batch size 256 achieves 69x higher maximum throughput than the baselines, which cannot exceed batch size 2.
OPT-30B: FlexGen 7.32 token/s versus 0.62 for Accelerate and 0.60 for DeepSpeed (prompt 512).
results.setup: OPT-30B, 1 T4, prompt 512, output 32, policy 48x3, 20% weights GPU 80% CPU, all KV cache and activations on CPU

results.claim: In the KV-cache memory analysis, OPT-175B at b=512, s=512, n=32 needs 1.2 TB of KV cache, 3.8x the model weights.
results.setup: OPT-175B FP16, l=96, h1=12288, h2=49152; KV cache peak 4*b*l*h1*(s+n) bytes; weights l(8h1^2+4h1h2) bytes
results.quote: the total memory required to store the KV cache is 1.2 TB, which is 3.8× the model weights

results.claim: Computing attention on the CPU when the KV cache is on the CPU cuts I/O by a factor of s, worthwhile for s of 512 or more.
results.setup: moved KV cache is b*s*h1*4 bytes versus moved activation b*h1*4 bytes
results.quote: so computing attention score on CPU reduces I/O by s×

results.claim: The zig-zag block schedule's I/O complexity is within 2x of optimal; the diagonal block schedule is asymptotically I/O-optimal but not implemented.
results.setup: theoretical proof, weights I/O, no CPU compute, infinite prompt stream (Appendix A.2)
results.quote: Theorem 4.1. The I/O complexity of the zig-zag block schedule is within 2× of the optimal solution.
results.note: A theoretical result (proof), not an experiment; kind set to measured only because no better label fits.

results.claim: 4-bit quantization of weights and KV cache loses little accuracy: OPT-175B Lambada 0.758 FP16 vs 0.756 4-bit; WikiText ppl 10.82 vs 10.94.

results.quote: Both methods show negligible accuracy loss compared to FP16.
results.table: Table 5, row OPT-175B, columns FP16 and 4-bit (Lambada acc 0.758, 0.756; WikiText ppl 10.82, 10.94)

results.claim: 3-bit compression did not preserve accuracy (no numbers given).
results.quote: We also tried 3-bit compression but it cannot preserve accuracy.

limits: Authors concede the cost-model policy can run out of memory (relaxation, fragmentation) and needs manual adjustment; a better policy can often be had by manual tuning.
Only the simpler zig-zag block schedule is implemented; the I/O-optimal diagonal block schedule is not, because it needs attention over non-contiguous KV memory.
Throughput comes at the cost of latency: batch latencies of thousands of seconds (e.g. 4000 to 11916 s for OPT-175B); only suitable for latency-insensitive batch work.
Only OPT models (6.7B to 175B) evaluated; applicability to GPT-3, PaLM, BLOOM is asserted, not tested. Throughput measured with dummy weights.
Only two baselines that support offloading, using row-by-row schedule, and quantization was not enabled in them.

Compression helps only large models that need offloading; at 1024 prompt on 6.7B FlexGen (c) is slightly below uncompressed (13.18 vs 13.72). CPU memory capacity is essential: RTX 3090 with 125 GB CPU memory does worse than the T4 with 208 GB on 30B and 175B.
Padding handles variable-length batches inefficiently; complementary techniques from Orca are suggested.
Sparse attention and quantization accuracy only checked on Lambada and WikiText for OPT-30B and OPT-175B; no seeds or variance reported.
Throughput numbers for the same setting differ by overhead tools (0.49 vs 0.69).
Dated: baselines (DeepSpeed ZeRO-Inference, Accelerate, Petals) are 2022 versions; the paper does not cover paged KV caches or continuous batching, though Orca is cited.

terms.definition: takes a prompt sequence to generate the key-value cache (KV cache) for each transformer layer of the LLM
utilizes and updates the KV cache to generate tokens step-by-step, where the current token generation depends on previously generated tokens
bn/t, the number of generated tokens divided by total latency for prefill plus decoding
the product of the GPU batch size and the number of GPU batches in a block
traverse the computational graph column-by-column within a block of batches so loaded layer weights are reused, stopping when activations and KV cache fill CPU and disk memory
batch LLM inference over a large number of tokens for back-of-house tasks that are less sensitive to latency
